title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 90
paragraphs: Such was the equipment of the Egyptians. The Cyprians furnished a hundred and fifty ships and were themselves equipped as follows: their kings had their heads wound with turbans, while the rest wore tunics; in other respects they were like the Greeks. Among these there are various races: some come from Salamis and Athens, others from Arcadia, others from Cythnus, others from Phoenicia, and still others from Ethiopia, as the Cyprians themselves report.
